setup.command: torchtitan Trainer with torchtitan_recipes.models.llama3.llama3_8b(seq_len=8192): FSDP 8 (fake process group, rank 0), 8192 tokens/microbatch, activation_remat=None, local_compile regions=[], deterministic=True, CUDA graphs off; profiled step 10 after 3 warmup steps

regions.title: Layer weight-gradient GEMMs writing fp32 directly into the reduce-scatter buffer
regions.description: The four weight-gradient GEMMs per layer write bf16 gradients that FSDP immediately re-reads to build the fp32 reduce-scatter input; their epilogues can write (bf16-rounded, widened) fp32 values at each rank's offset of the reduce-scatter buffer.
regions.bitwise_notes: Epilogue must round each gradient to bf16 before widening to fp32 to match eager (wgrad in bf16, then chunk_cat upcast).
regions.dataflow: Each weight gradient is consumed only by the reduce-scatter copy-in (AccumulateGrad is a no-op hand-off).
regions.blockers: Requires FSDP to expose its reduce-scatter buffer before backward and GEMMs with a row-blocked scattered output layout (each rank's slice is a separate address range).

regions.title: w2 dgrad GEMM with SwiGLU-backward epilogue
regions.description: The w2 input-gradient GEMM produces dh [8192,14336]; its epilogue can load gate_up and write the stacked [8192,28672] SwiGLU gradient directly.
regions.bitwise_notes: GEMM output must be rounded to bf16 (dh) before the pointwise backward math.
regions.dataflow: dh is consumed only by the SwiGLU backward.
regions.blockers: Custom GEMM epilogue with two extra operand loads; bitwise main loop.

regions.title: FSDP reduce-scatter copy-in: w13 grad re-layout + bf16->fp32 chunk_cat
regions.description: Per layer, the bf16 weight gradients (wqkv, wo, w13 [2,14336,4096], w2, two norms) are first re-laid out (w13 chunked along dim 1 and concatenated to [16,1792,4096]) and then copied with an fp32 upcast into the [8, 27.26M] reduce-scatter input; one pass can write the fp32 buffer straight from the gradients.
regions.bitwise_notes: Pure data movement with an exact bf16->fp32 widening; bitwise identical as long as every element lands in the same rank-major slot.
regions.dataflow: cat output [16,1792,4096] bf16 is consumed only by _chunk_cat, whose output is consumed only by the reduce-scatter; both are index permutations plus a cast of the same 218M gradient elements.
regions.blockers: Owned by FSDP2 (foreach_reduce / chunk_cat); the Shard(1) w13 path is a separate cat before the chunk_cat. Needs a custom copy-in kernel or a chunk_cat that accepts a per-parameter shard dim.
regions.notes: chunk_cat runs at ~2.2 TB/s and the Shard(1) cat at ~1.2 TB/s; the fused ideal is 189 us/layer.

regions.title: SwiGLU backward: two muls, silu_backward and the gate/up gradient cat in one pass
regions.description: Backward of SwiGLU computes d_up = dh * silu(gate), d_silu = dh * up, d_gate = silu_backward(d_silu, gate) and stacks d_gate and d_up into [8192,28672]; one kernel reads dh and gate_up and writes the stacked gradient directly.
regions.bitwise_notes: Pointwise with bf16 roundings at the same points as eager (d_up = dh*silu(gate), d_silu = dh*up, silu_backward in fp32).
regions.dataflow: The two mul outputs and silu_backward output feed only the UnbindBackward0 cat, whose output feeds only w13's backward GEMMs. Recomputing silu(gate) from gate_up removes the forward's saved silu output (forward-backward pairing).
regions.blockers: Autograd materializes each gradient separately and stacks them with cat; needs a custom autograd Function (as the local_compile region would provide).

regions.title: SwiGLU computed in the w2 GEMM A-operand prologue
regions.description: Instead of writing h = silu(gate)*up [8192,14336] and reading it back, the w2 projection can compute h tile by tile while loading its A operand from gate_up.
regions.bitwise_notes: Prologue must produce the same bf16 h values (silu in fp32, bf16 round, multiply, bf16 round) before feeding the MMA.
regions.dataflow: h is consumed by the w2 GEMM and saved for w2's weight gradient; recomputing h from the saved gate_up in backward removes the saved copy (forward-backward pairing).
regions.blockers: h is also needed by w2's weight-gradient GEMM in backward: either still write h (costs 235 MB, stays flop-bound) or recompute it in the backward prologue. Needs a GEMM with a fused elementwise A-prologue.
regions.notes: Alternative to R-06 (epilogue of w13); only one of the two can own the SwiGLU.

regions.title: SwiGLU forward: silu(gate) * up in one pass
regions.description: In each feed_forward, silu reads the strided gate half of w13's [8192,2,14336] output and writes a [8192,14336] bf16 tensor that mul immediately reads with the up half; one kernel reads gate_up once and writes the product.
regions.bitwise_notes: Pointwise; reproduce silu in fp32 then bf16 rounding of silu(gate) before the multiply.
regions.dataflow: silu output is consumed by mul (and saved for MulBackward0); gate and up come from the same w13 output.
regions.blockers: Eager runs two ATen kernels on a non-contiguous gate view (non-vectorized path, ~1.7 TB/s). The recipe's default local_compile region 'fused_binary_activation' covers this but is off in this run.
regions.notes: Ideal assumes the backward recomputes silu(gate) instead of reading a saved copy (see R-05).

regions.title: w13 GEMM with SwiGLU epilogue
regions.description: The w13 projection [8192,4096]x[4096,28672] can apply silu(gate)*up in its epilogue, writing gate_up (saved for backward) and h without a separate pass.
regions.bitwise_notes: Epilogue must round the GEMM accumulator to bf16 before silu (as eager does) and keep the same GEMM K-order.
regions.dataflow: w13 output feeds only the SwiGLU (and is saved for its backward).
regions.blockers: Needs a GEMM with a paired-column epilogue (gate and up columns 14336 apart) and bitwise-identical main loop to cuBLAS/nvjet.
regions.notes: Measured w13 GEMM already runs above the random-data peak (low-entropy fake-PG data), so most of the gap is the SwiGLU pass.

regions.title: Fused linear cross-entropy (lm_head forward + CE + lm_head dgrad) per chunk
regions.description: Per chunk, lm_head [1024,4096]x[4096,128256] produces logits that only feed the CE, and the CE gradient feeds only lm_head's input-gradient GEMM; a fused linear-CE never writes the 263 MB bf16 logits or the fp32 intermediates.
regions.bitwise_notes: Needs both GEMMs and the vocab reduction inside; logits are never materialized, so bitwise needs the same per-tile reduction order as the unfused path (hard).
regions.dataflow: logits -> CE -> dlogits -> dgrad GEMM; nothing else reads logits/dlogits (dlogits also feeds the weight-gradient GEMM, R-19).
regions.blockers: dlogits is also needed by the lm_head weight-gradient GEMM; a fused kernel must either recompute logits for it or emit dlogits. Bitwise is very hard.

regions.title: Cross-entropy forward + backward per loss chunk
regions.description: For each 1024-token chunk, the [1024,128256] bf16 logits are upcast to fp32, log_softmax'd, gathered by nll, then backward zeroes a fp32 gradient, scatters, runs log_softmax backward and casts back to bf16; a single fused CE kernel reads the bf16 logits once and writes bf16 dlogits plus the scalar loss.
regions.shapes_dtypes: logits bf16 [1024,128256] (+fp32 copy, log-probs, fp32 grad), labels int64 [1024] -> dlogits bf16 [1024,128256]
regions.bitwise_notes: logsumexp over V=128256 in fp32 must reproduce PyTorch's log_softmax reduction tree; the nll gather/scatter and the 1/num_tokens scaling are pointwise.
regions.dataflow: The fp32 logits, log-probs and fp32 dlogits are each consumed by exactly the next op; the chunk's backward runs immediately after its forward, so forward and backward can share one kernel.
regions.blockers: CrossEntropyLoss is compiled by the 'loss' local_compile region in the default recipe (off here); bitwise reduction order over the vocab.
regions.notes: Members include the per-chunk scalar ops (div by token count, loss accumulation, ones_like seed) and the total_loss zero init.

regions.title: wqkv GEMM with split + RoPE epilogue
regions.description: The fused qkv projection can write q, k (rotated) and v in their separate contiguous layouts from its epilogue.
regions.bitwise_notes: Epilogue rounds to bf16 before the fp32 rotation, matching eager.
regions.dataflow: wqkv output feeds only the split/rope chain.
regions.blockers: Custom epilogue with a position-indexed cache load and head-dependent output routing.

regions.title: QKV split copies + complex RoPE forward in one pass
regions.description: After wqkv, q is made contiguous, k and v are copied, and RoPE upcasts q and k to fp32, multiplies by the complex cache gathered at positions, and casts back; one kernel can read the fused [8192,6144] qkv once and write rotated q, rotated k and v.
regions.bitwise_notes: Pointwise; the fp32 complex multiply must use the same operation order/FMA contraction as the eager complex-mul kernel (the compiled real-arithmetic path is only within 1 bf16 ulp).
regions.dataflow: Each copy/cast output is consumed only by the next op in the chain; q and k use the same gathered cache rows (horizontal), v only needs the copy.
regions.blockers: Eager ComplexRoPE uses view_as_complex/complex mul; the 'rope' local_compile region is off here. Bitwise needs matching the complex multiply arithmetic.

regions.title: FSDP all-gather copy-out: split_with_sizes_copy + w13 Shard(1) re-assembly
regions.description: After each layer's all-gather (forward and backward prefetch), the [8, 27.26M] bf16 buffer is split into per-parameter tensors and w13 is then re-assembled by a second cat from its eight [2,1792,4096] shards; the copy-out can write w13 in its final [2,14336,4096] layout directly.
regions.bitwise_notes: Order-sensitive copy only (no arithmetic); bitwise trivially once indices match.
regions.dataflow: split_with_sizes_copy writes w13's per-rank pieces into a temporary [8,2*7340032] view that only the following cat reads.
regions.blockers: FSDP2 copy-out path (split_with_sizes_copy + Shard(dim!=0) fix-up) is library-owned; needs a copy-out that handles non-zero shard dims in one pass.
regions.notes: 64 instances = 32 forward + 32 backward re-gathers (reshard after forward).

regions.title: RoPE backward + dQKV assembly in one pass
regions.description: Backward of RoPE upcasts dq and dk to fp32, multiplies by the conjugated cache, casts back to bf16, and SplitWithSizesBackward concatenates dq, dk, dv into [8192,8,6,128]; one kernel can read dq/dk/dv and write the fused dqkv.
regions.bitwise_notes: Pointwise conj-multiply in fp32 plus casts; same arithmetic-order caveat as R-08.
regions.dataflow: Each cast/mul output is consumed only by the next op; the final cat feeds only wqkv's backward GEMMs.
regions.blockers: Autograd materializes each step; needs a custom autograd Function for the rope+split.
regions.notes: Could additionally absorb the flash-attention backward postprocess (fp32 dq/dk/dv accumulators -> bf16), see R-16.

regions.title: FSDP all-gather copy-in: cast each layer's fp32 shard once per step, reuse it for the backward re-gather
regions.description: Each layer's fp32 parameter shard is cast to bf16 and copied into the all-gather input twice per step (forward gather and backward re-gather) with identical results; casting once into a persistent per-layer bf16 all-gather input removes the backward pair of copies.
regions.shapes_dtypes: layer shard fp32 [27264000] -> bf16 all-gather input [27264000], 2 gathers per step
regions.bitwise_notes: The fp32 shard does not change between forward and backward of a step, so the cached bf16 values are bitwise identical.
regions.dataflow: Forward and backward copy-in read the same unchanged fp32 shard and write the same bf16 all-gather input values.
regions.blockers: Keeping the bf16 all-gather input (54.5 MB per layer, 1.7 GB for 32 layers) alive from forward to backward trades memory for the copies; FSDP2 frees it after each all-gather.
regions.notes: Covers the 32 decoder layers only (the 64 layer instances of R-03); ideal is one cast+copy per layer per step.

regions.title: RMSNorm backward + residual-gradient accumulation
regions.description: Each norm backward writes dx [8192,4096] and then add_ accumulates it into the residual gradient; the norm backward can add the incoming residual gradient in its epilogue and write the sum once.
regions.bitwise_notes: Row reductions (dot(dy*w, x)) and the weight-gradient column reduction must follow the quack kernel's order.
regions.dataflow: The norm's dx is consumed only by the add_ into the residual-gradient buffer.
regions.blockers: Autograd accumulates the two gradient contributions of the residual stream with a separate add_; needs a fused norm-backward-with-residual Function.

regions.title: lm_head weight gradient: one GEMM over all chunks writing the reduce-scatter buffer
regions.description: The eight chunk weight-gradient GEMMs ([128256,1024]x[1024,4096], first mm then 7 addmm) each read and write the full fp32 [128256,4096] accumulator (4.2 GB per chunk), which is then copied unchanged into the reduce-scatter buffer; one K=8192 GEMM (or a persistent accumulator that is the reduce-scatter buffer) avoids both.
regions.bitwise_notes: Changes the fp32 accumulation order from 8 sequential K=1024 GEMMs (addmm into fp32) to one K=8192 GEMM; bitwise only if the GEMM keeps the same per-chunk accumulation order.
regions.dataflow: All eight GEMMs write the same accumulator, consumed only by the reduce-scatter copy-in, whose dim-0 chunking of a contiguous [128256,4096] tensor is a no-op layout change.
regions.blockers: Batching needs all eight chunks' bf16 dlogits (2.1 GB) alive at once, against the purpose of the chunked loss; aliasing the accumulator to FSDP's reduce-scatter buffer needs FSDP API support.

regions.title: FSDP all-gather copy-in: fp32->bf16 cast fused with copy into all-gather buffer
regions.description: Before every all-gather the fp32 sharded parameters are cast to bf16 into temporaries and then copied into the flat all-gather input buffer; a single foreach kernel can cast straight into the buffer.
regions.shapes_dtypes: layer shard fp32 27.26M elems -> bf16 all-gather input; tok_embeddings / (norm, lm_head) shards 65.7M elems
regions.bitwise_notes: Elementwise round-to-nearest bf16 cast and a copy; bitwise identical.
regions.dataflow: The bf16 temporaries written by the first _foreach_copy_ are read only by the all_gather_copy_in _foreach_copy_.
regions.blockers: FSDP2 mixed-precision cast (FSDPParam.all_gather_inputs) and copy-in are separate library steps.
regions.notes: Instances: 34 forward (tok_embeddings, 32 layers, norm+lm_head) + 33 backward (32 layer prefetches + norm+lm_head re-gather).

regions.title: Residual adds as wo / w2 GEMM epilogues
regions.description: Both residual adds of each block (x + wo(...), h + w2(...)) can be done in the epilogue of the GEMM producing the branch output, avoiding the separate read of the branch output and the residual.
regions.bitwise_notes: Epilogue must round the accumulator to bf16 first and then add the bf16 residual in fp32 to match eager's two roundings.
regions.dataflow: wo and w2 outputs are consumed only by the residual adds.
regions.blockers: Custom epilogue; alternative to R-12/R-13 (fuse the add into the following norm instead).
regions.notes: Per-instance values are averages of the wo and w2 instances; ideal is flop-bound so the gap is mostly the add kernel plus GEMM-vs-peak differences.

regions.title: Embedding backward writing fp32 straight into the reduce-scatter buffer
regions.description: The embedding backward zero-fills a 1.05 GB bf16 [128256,4096] gradient, scatter-adds the 8192 token gradients (sort + segment sum), and FSDP then copies it with an fp32 upcast into the reduce-scatter buffer; one pass can zero-fill and scatter directly into the fp32 buffer.
regions.bitwise_notes: Deterministic sorted segment sums in bf16 (same token grouping and order), then an exact widening to fp32.
regions.dataflow: The bf16 embedding gradient is consumed only by the reduce-scatter copy-in.
regions.blockers: embedding_dense_backward (deterministic) and FSDP's chunk_cat are separate library steps; bitwise requires the bf16 segment-sum rounding before widening.

regions.title: Flash-attention backward prologue/epilogue kernels folded into neighbours
regions.description: Around each attention backward, accumulators are zeroed by memsets, a preprocess kernel computes rowsum(dO*O) (and zeroes dQ accumulation), and three postprocess kernels convert fp32 dQ/dK/dV accumulators to bf16; these can be folded into the wo dgrad epilogue (rowsum) and the RoPE-backward pass (conversion).
regions.shapes_dtypes: O, dO bf16 [8192,32,128]; dQ accum fp32 [8192,32,128]; dK/dV accum fp32
regions.bitwise_notes: Inside the attention library; the dQ fp32 accumulation order is set by the main kernel and must be preserved.
regions.dataflow: dO (wo dgrad output) and O feed the preprocess; the postprocess outputs feed only RoPE backward / the dqkv cat.
regions.blockers: Library-owned (flash_attn.cute via torch varlen_attn); changing the kernel boundary needs the library to expose fp32 accumulators or accept a fused epilogue.
regions.notes: Measured times are the memset, preprocess and postprocess kernels only (main attention kernels excluded). Ideal bytes are estimated from the kernels' tensor shapes (accumulator layout assumed unpadded).

regions.title: lm_head grad accumulator aliased to the reduce-scatter buffer (last chunk GEMM + copy)
regions.description: The fp32 lm_head gradient [128256,4096] is copied by chunk_cat into an [8,65667072] buffer with the identical memory layout; letting the last chunk's addmm accumulate in (or the accumulator be) that buffer removes the 4.2 GB copy.
regions.bitwise_notes: Removes a byte-for-byte fp32 copy; the GEMM is unchanged, so numerics are unchanged.
regions.dataflow: chunk_cat input is the final accumulator and its output feeds only the reduce-scatter.
regions.blockers: Requires FSDP to accept a pre-placed gradient in its reduce-scatter buffer (or to skip chunk_cat when the layout already matches).

regions.title: Varlen attention metadata (cu_seqlens) from positions in one kernel
regions.description: Before the forward, the decoder builds packed cu_seqlens from positions with ~25 tiny ops (eq, cumsum, where, full, arange, scatter_, sums and async asserts); with deterministic algorithms scatter_ becomes a sort-based index_put taking ~0.65 ms for 8192 elements.
regions.bitwise_notes: Integer cumsum/scatter; exact. scatter_ order only matters for the discarded overflow slot.
regions.dataflow: All intermediates are consumed within the metadata builder; output is a [19] int32 cu_seqlens.
regions.blockers: Deterministic mode routes scatter_ through index_put_ with sorting; a dedicated kernel (or a non-scatter formulation) is needed.

regions.title: RoPE cache gather, position bounds check and cache conj computed once per step
regions.description: Every layer re-checks positions <= max position, gathers cache[positions] into [8192,1,64] complex64, and in backward re-materializes the conjugated cache twice; these depend only on positions and are identical for all 32 layers.
regions.bitwise_notes: Pure gathers/compares/conj; bitwise identical.
regions.dataflow: positions and the rope cache are the same tensors for every layer; the gathered cache and its conj have no layer-dependent input.
regions.blockers: Each layer owns its RoPE module and cache buffer; hoisting needs the decoder to precompute the gathered cache (or the fused rope kernel to gather inline, which R-08/R-10 already assume).
regions.notes: Ideal per instance is the once-per-step cost divided by 32.

regions.title: Attention residual add + ffn_norm RMSNorm
regions.description: h = x + attn_out is written to memory and immediately re-read by ffn_norm; a fused add+RMSNorm reads x and attn_out once and writes h (residual) and the normalized [8192,4096] output.
regions.bitwise_notes: RMSNorm's row sum of squares must use the same reduction order as the existing quack RMSNorm kernel.
regions.dataflow: h feeds ffn_norm and the next residual add; attn_out (wo output) feeds only the add.
regions.blockers: Bitwise match of the quack RMSNorm reduction; the add sits in the block's forward between two modules.

regions.title: FFN residual add + next layer's attention_norm (or final norm)
regions.description: The block output h + ffn_out of layer i is written and immediately normalized by layer i+1's attention_norm (the final model norm after layer 31); fusing the add into the next norm saves a write+read of [8192,4096].
regions.bitwise_notes: Same reduction-order requirement as R-12.
regions.dataflow: The block output feeds the next block's attention_norm and its residual add only.
regions.blockers: Crosses the transformer-block (and FSDP unit) boundary; eager module structure keeps them in different module calls.

regions.title: Final norm backward fused with the chunked-loss gradient accumulation
regions.description: The chunked loss zero-fills an [8192,4096] gradient buffer and copies each chunk's hidden-state gradient into it, then the final RMSNorm backward reads it; the norm backward can consume the chunk gradients directly (row-wise), so the buffer fill and copies disappear.
regions.bitwise_notes: Norm weight-gradient reduction over 8192 rows must keep the quack kernel's order; row-wise dx is order-free.
regions.dataflow: The accumulation buffer is written by 8 copies and read once by the final norm's backward.
regions.blockers: The chunk loop and the decoder backward are separate autograd graphs joined by _DecoderOutputGradientBackProp; the norm's weight gradient needs a cross-chunk reduction.

regions.title: Token embedding gather + layer-0 attention_norm
regions.description: The embedding gather writes h0 [8192,4096] which layer 0's attention_norm immediately re-reads; the norm can gather rows directly (still writing h0 for the residual).
regions.bitwise_notes: RMSNorm reduction order.
regions.dataflow: h0 feeds attention_norm and the first residual add.
regions.blockers: Crosses the embedding/decoder-layer and FSDP unit boundary.

no_opportunity.what: backward layers.* host-to-device metadata memcpy (FSDP) x64
no_opportunity.reason: Host-to-device copies of FSDP split-size / chunk metadata (int64 [3831], [53288]); launch-latency bound, no device dataflow to fuse with. Removable only by caching the metadata on device.

Single-kernel FSDP all-gather copy-out for groups without Shard(dim!=0) parameters (tok_embeddings, norm+lm_head); already one pass at ~6.8 TB/s (ideal 304 us vs 309 us measured). The backward re-gather of (norm, lm_head) only serves the norm weight -- a grouping issue, not a fusion one.
